item.title: Rocket Report: Lightning strikes in China; Starship launch on deck (로켓 리포트: 중국에 번개가 치다; 갑판 위 스타쉽 발사)
item.description:
Relativity Space announced plans to build a second rocket factory near Cape Canaveral, Florida.
(리타티비티 스페이스는 플로리다 케이프 커내버럴 근처에 두 번째 로켓 공장을 건설할 계획을 발표했습니다.)

Welcome to Edition 9.04 of the Rocket Report! We’ve had to wait an extra week for SpaceX to get its 13th Starship test flight off the ground. A last-second abort on July 16 led engineers to roll the booster back to its hangar in South Texas to swap out engines. Starship is now back on the launch pad. Liftoff is set for Friday evening. A flawless launch and reentry will put SpaceX on the cusp of an orbital flight later this year. Ars will have a comprehensive recap story after the completion of the test flight.
(로켓 리포트 9.04호에 오신 것을 환영합니다! 스페이스X가 13번째 스타쉽 시험 비행을 시작하기 위해 일주일을 더 기다려야 했습니다. 7월 16일 마지막 순간의 중단으로 엔지니어들은 부스터를 남부 텍사스의 격납고로 다시 옮겨 엔진을 교체했다. 스타쉽이 다시 발사대에 도착했습니다. 발사는 금요일 저녁으로 예정되어 있습니다. 완벽한 발사와 재진입은 올해 말 스페이스X를 궤도 비행 직전으로 이끌 것입니다. Ars는 시험 비행 완료 후 포괄적인 요약 기사를 전할 예정입니다.)

As always, we welcome reader submissions . If you don’t want to miss an issue, please subscribe using the box below (the form will not appear on AMP-enabled versions of the site). Each report will include information on small-, medium-, and heavy-lift rockets, as well as a quick look ahead at the next three launches on the calendar.
(항상 그렇듯이, 독자 여러분의 의견 제출을 환영합니다. 이슈를 놓치고 싶지 않으시면 아래 박스를 통해 구독해 주세요(AMP 지원 버전에서는 이 양식이 나타나지 않습니다). 각 보고서에는 소형, 중형, 중량 로켓에 대한 정보와 앞으로 예정된 세 차례 발사에 대한 간단한 안내가 포함될 예정입니다.)

India’s first private rocket reaches orbit. Indian space officials celebrated the debut flight of Skyroot Aerospace’s Vikram-1 rocket, India’s first fully commercial satellite launcher, as a “grand success” Saturday after an on-target climb into a 280-mile-high orbit following liftoff from an island spaceport in the Bay of Bengal, Ars reports . The Vikram-1 lifted off from India’s primary spaceport on Sriharikota Island around midday local time. The launch was delayed more than a half-hour to resolve a last-minute technical problem. The countdown resumed, culminating in the command to ignite Vikram-1’s solid-fueled first stage booster to propel the rocket off the launch pad.
(인도 최초의 민간 로켓이 궤도에 진입했다. 인도 우주 관계자들은 벵골만의 섬 우주항에서 발사된 후 목표에 맞춰 280마일 고도 궤도에 진입한 후 스카이루트 에어로스페이스의 빅람-1 로켓의 첫 비행을 "대성공"으로 축하했다고 Ars가 보도했다. 비크람-1은 현지 시각 정오경 인도의 주요 우주항인 스리하리코타 섬에서 이륙했다. 마지막 순간의 기술적 문제 해결로 발사가 30분 이상 지연되었다. 카운트다운이 재개되었고, 빅람-1의 고체 연료 1단 부스터를 점화해 로켓을 발사대에서 이륙시키라는 명령으로 절정에 달했다.)

Right on the money… Vikram-1 is modest in size compared to India’s larger workhorse rockets. Skyroot’s rocket stands about 72 feet (22 meters) tall, with the capability to place payloads of up to 770 pounds (350 kilograms) into low-Earth orbit. This makes Vikram-1 somewhat larger than the Electron launch vehicle developed by Rocket Lab, the world’s most successful dedicated small satellite launcher. The flight on Saturday went off without any major problems. Three solid-fueled rocket motors fired in succession to reach space, then a small liquid-fueled fourth stage ignited and accelerated to orbital velocity, some 17,000 mph. The rocket reached an orbit approximately 280 miles (450 kilometers) high at an inclination of 60 degrees to the equator, quite close to preflight predictions. (submitted by Astroman)
(정확히 맞아... 빅람-1은 인도의 대형 주력 로켓에 비해 크기가 적당하다. 스카이루트의 로켓은 약 72피트(22미터) 높이이며, 최대 770파운드(350킬로그램)의 탑재물을 저지구 궤도에 투입할 수 있습니다. 이로 인해 빅람-1은 세계에서 가장 성공적인 전용 소형 위성 발사체인 로켓 랩에서 개발한 일렉트론 발사체보다 다소 큽니다. 토요일 비행은 큰 문제 없이 출발했습니다. 세 개의 고체 연료 로켓 모터가 연속으로 점화되어 우주에 도달했고, 이어 소형 액체 연료 4단이 점화되어 약 17,000 mph의 궤도 속도로 가속했다. 로켓은 적도 방향 60도 경사로 약 280마일(450킬로미터) 높이의 궤도에 도달했으며, 이는 사전 비행 예측과 매우 근접한 수준이었다. (아스트로맨이 제출))

US seeks ideas on offshore launch. The Interior Department wants the public to weigh in on one idea for what to do with hundreds of inactive offshore oil platforms, The Washington Post reports . Could they be turned into launch pads for rockets to space? The department’s Bureau of Ocean Energy Management issued a request for public comment earlier this month, “intended to inform BOEM’s understanding of technical, environmental, operational, legal, regulatory, and interagency considerations,” without proposing any specific policy action. The government is looking for ideas on how to ease congestion at the nation’s spaceports while also developing additional launch sites to make the country’s space transport infrastructure more resilient to potential attack.
(미국은 해상 발사에 대한 아이디어를 모색하고 있습니다. 내무부는 수백 개의 비활성 해상 석유 플랫폼을 어떻게 처리할지에 대해 국민의 의견을 내고자 한다고 워싱턴 포스트가 보도했습니다. 이 다리들이 우주로 가는 로켓의 발사대로 전환될 수 있을까요? 국방부 산하 해양 에너지 관리국은 이달 초 공개 의견 수렴 요청을 발표했는데, 이는 "기술적, 환경적, 운영적, 법적, 규제적, 부처 간 고려사항에 대한 BOEM의 이해를 알리기 위한 것"이지만, 구체적인 정책 조치는 제안하지 않았다. 정부는 국가 우주항의 혼잡을 완화하는 동시에, 잠재적 공격에 대한 우주 운송 인프라를 강화하기 위해 추가 발사장 개발에 대한 아이디어를 모색하고 있다.)

Not a crazy idea. .. “It’s actually not as crazy of an idea as you might think,” said George Nield, a consultant and former Federal Aviation Administration official who oversaw commercial space transportation. “We’re running out of space and places to be able to fly from.” Rockets have launched from a converted oil platform before. The most successful offshore launch venture was Sea Launch, which used a modified oil-drilling rig as the departure point for 36 satellite launches from 1999 through 2014.
(무리한 생각은 아니에요. .. "사실 생각만큼 미친 생각은 아닙니다,"라고 컨설턴트이자 전 연방항공국(FAA) 관리인 조지 닐드는 상업 우주 운송을 감독했습니다. "공간도 없고 날아갈 곳도 부족해." 이전에도 개조된 석유 플랫폼에서 로켓이 발사된 적이 있습니다. 가장 성공적인 해상 발사 사업은 Sea Launch로, 1999년부터 2014년까지 36회의 위성 발사를 개조된 석유 시추 시추 시추 지점으로 사용했습니다.)

Lockheed interested in RDREs. Venus Aerospace and Lockheed Martin have entered a collaboration agreement for the evaluation of Houston-based Venus’s rotating detonation rocket engine (RDRE) technology, Aviation Week & Space Technology reports . The companies hope to achieve “precision fire” capabilities with efficiencies that translate into longer flight ranges and higher speeds. Lockheed Martin is the Pentagon’s largest contractor, responsible for supplying the military with thousands of tactical and strategic missiles. Venus Aerospace’s RDRE tech works by generating thrust as a wave of detonation travels around a circular channel, sustained by the injection of fuel and oxidizer to produce a supersonic shockwave. The company completed a low-altitude flight test of the RDRE last year.
(록히드는 RDRE에 관심이 많았습니다. Aviation Week and Space Technology에 따르면, Venus Aerospace와 Lockheed Martin은 휴스턴에 본사를 둔 Venus의 회전 폭발 로켓 엔진(RDRE) 기술 평가를 위한 협력 계약을 체결했습니다. 양사들은 더 긴 비행 거리와 더 높은 속도를 실현하는 효율적인 '정밀 사격' 능력을 달성하기를 희망하고 있습니다. 록히드 마틴은 펜타곤 최대 계약업체로, 군에 수천 기의 전술 및 전략 미사일을 공급하는 책임을 맡고 있다. Venus Aerospace의 RDRE 기술은 폭발파가 원형 채널을 따라 이동하면서 추력을 생성하고, 연료와 산화제를 주입해 초음속 충격파를 발생시킵니다. 이 회사는 작년에 RDRE의 저고도 비행 시험을 완료했습니다.)

Improved efficiency. .. The agreement with Venus Aerospace “enables Lockheed Martin to evaluate RDRE technology within the context of operational military requirements to transition the advanced propulsion concept from a subsystem demonstration environment into practical missile applications,” Lockheed Martin said in a statement. The RDRE architecture has the potential to improve propulsion efficiency while reducing complexity. There’s a lot of work to do to scale Venus’s engine from an experimental prototype to a combat-ready missile platform.
(효율성 향상. .. 록히드 마틴은 성명에서 "비너스 에어로스페이스와의 협약은 록히드 마틴이 RDRE 기술을 군사 작전 요구사항 맥락에서 평가하여 첨단 추진 개념을 하위 시스템 시범 환경에서 실용적인 미사일 응용으로 전환할 수 있게 한다"고 밝혔다. RDRE 아키텍처는 복잡성을 줄이면서 추진 효율을 향상시킬 잠재력을 가지고 있습니다. 비너스의 엔진을 실험용 프로토타입에서 전투 준비가 된 미사일 플랫폼으로 확장하려면 해야 할 일이 많습니다.)

Will Amur ever fly? Nearly six years have passed since the state-backed Russian space corporation, Roscosmos, unveiled plans to develop a reusable rocket called “Amur-LNG.” Clearly designed in response to SpaceX’s Falcon 9 rocket, Amur was intended to have a reusable first stage, methane-powered engines, and the capability to deliver 10.5 metric tons to low-Earth orbit in reusable mode. At the time, Russian space officials said they planned to debut the rocket in 2026, so basically right about now. The latest update from Roscosmos suggests the Amur rocket won’t begin flight tests until 2031, Ars reports .
(아무르는 과연 날아올까? 국가가 지원하는 러시아 우주기업 로스코스모스가 "아무르-LNG"라는 재사용 로켓 개발 계획을 발표한 지 거의 6년이 지났다. 명백히 스페이스X의 팔콘 9 로켓에 대응해 설계된 아무르는 재사용 가능한 1단, 메탄 추진 엔진, 그리고 재사용 모드에서 저지구 궤도에 10.5미터톤을 투입할 수 있는 능력을 갖추도록 설계되었습니다. 당시 러시아 우주 관계자들은 2026년에 로켓을 데뷔시킬 계획이라고 밝혔으니, 사실상 지금쯤입니다. 로스코스모스의 최신 업데이트에 따르면 아무르 로켓은 2031년까지 비행 시험을 시작할 수 없다고 Ars가 보도했습니다.)

Year for year. .. To summarize, when the Amur rocket was announced in 2020, its flight date was scheduled for 2026. Some six years later, its projected launch date has moved five years into the future. The only reasonable conclusion is that Russia’s answer to the Falcon 9 rocket will not arrive any time soon, and it is unlikely to do so until at least two decades after SpaceX first landed an orbital rocket.
(해마다 마찬가지입니다. .. 요약하자면, 2020년 아무르 로켓이 발표되었을 때, 비행일은 2026년으로 예정되어 있었습니다. 약 6년 후, 예정된 발사일은 5년 후로 미뤄졌습니다. 유일한 합리적인 결론은 러시아의 팔콘 9 로켓 대응책이 당분간 도착하지 않을 것이며, 스페이스X가 궤도 로켓을 처음 착륙시킨 지 최소 20년이 지나야 도착할 가능성이 높다는 점이다.)

Space Force to buy more launches. It seems as though $5.6 billion wasn’t enough. That was the news from the US Space Force on Friday, July 17, when military officials announced they were tripling the maximum value of one of the service’s National Security Space Launch contracts to $17 billion, Ars reports . The expansion of the Space Force’s National Security Space Launch (NSSL) Phase 3 contract comes as the Pentagon signals rising demand for military satellite launches. The NSSL program is set up to allow Space Systems Command, which oversees the Space Force’s launch program, to select from a pool of launch providers for individual missions to deliver the military’s satellites to orbit.
(스페이스 포스가 더 많은 발사를 구매하는 것. 56억 달러로는 부족한 것 같습니다. 이것이 7월 17일 금요일 미 우주군에서 전한 소식으로, 군 관계자들이 국가안보 우주발사 계약 중 하나의 최대 가치를 170억 달러로 세 배로 늘리겠다고 발표했다고 Ars가 보도했습니다. 우주군의 국가안보우주발사(NSSL) 3단계 계약 확대는 국방부가 군사 위성 발사 수요 증가를 신호하는 가운데 이루어졌습니다. NSSL 프로그램은 우주군 발사 프로그램을 감독하는 우주 시스템 사령부가 개별 임무를 위한 발사 제공자 풀 중에서 선별하여 군 위성을 궤도에 올릴 수 있도록 설계되었습니다.)

Appetizing … The $17 billion portion covers just one part of the NSSL Phase 3 program. This segment, known as Lane 1, covers a subset of the Space Force’s more risk-tolerant missions. Lane 2 includes more expensive strategic satellites and carries a maximum value of $13.7 billion, a number sufficient to cover an estimated 54 launches projected for procurement through 2029. In April, Space Systems Command said it had identified 25 additional Lane 2 missions on top of the 54 included in the original contract just one year before. Now, the Space Force is tripling the maximum value for the Lane 1 contract. With last week’s announcement, the combined maximum value of Lane 1 and Lane 2 has reached more than $30 billion, and the number is likely to climb again. (submitted by biokleen)
(맛있다... 170억 달러 규모의 부분은 NSSL 3단계 프로그램의 한 부분만을 다룹니다. 이 구간은 레인 1(Lane 1)으로 알려져 있으며, 우주군의 더 위험 감수 능력이 강한 임무 일부를 다룹니다. 레인 2에는 더 비싼 전략 위성이 포함되어 있으며, 최대 가치는 137억 달러로, 2029년까지 조달 예정인 약 54회의 발사를 감당할 수 있는 금액이다. 4월에 우주 시스템 사령부는 1년 전 원래 계약에 포함된 54개 임무 외에 추가로 25개의 레인 2 임무를 확인했다고 밝혔다. 이제 우주군이 레인 1 계약의 최대 가치를 세 배로 늘리고 있습니다. 지난주 발표로 1번 레인과 2번 레인의 합산 최대 가치는 300억 달러를 넘었으며, 앞으로 더 오를 가능성이 큽니다. (바이오클리언 제출))

Robotic servicing mission launches from Cape Canaveral. A spacecraft fitted with two flexible robotic arms is on the way to geosynchronous orbit after launching earlier this week on a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket, kicking off a planned decade-long mission to open new frontiers in satellite servicing, Ars reports. The Mission Robotic Vehicle, owned and built by Northrop Grumman, rocketed into orbit from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida on Tuesday. Three small propulsion pods, each functioning as standalone spacecraft, accompanied the MRV aboard the Falcon 9 rocket.
(케이프 커내버럴에서 로봇 정비 임무가 발사됩니다. 두 개의 유연한 로봇 팔을 장착한 우주선이 이번 주 초 스페이스X 팔콘 9 로켓으로 발사된 후 정지궤도에 진입 중이며, 이는 위성 서비스 분야에서 새로운 영역을 개척하는 10년간의 예정된 임무를 시작했다고 Ars가 보도했다. 노스럽 그루먼이 소유하고 제작한 미션 로봇 차량이 화요일 플로리다의 케이프 커내버럴 우주군 기지에서 궤도에 진입했습니다. 각각 독립적인 우주선으로 작동하는 세 개의 소형 추진 포드가 MRV와 함께 팰컨 9 로켓에 탑재되었다.)

First of its kind … The Mission Robotic Vehicle is arguably the most advanced servicing satellite ever launched. It’s certainly the most sophisticated orbiting servicer we know anything about. Developed in a public-private partnership between Northrop Grumman and DARPA, the MRV uses its two robotic arms to install the propulsion pods onto other satellites in geosynchronous orbit and extend their lives.
(처음으로 ... 미션 로봇 차량은 아마도 지금까지 발사된 가장 진보된 서비스 위성일 것입니다. 우리가 아는 한 가장 정교한 궤도 서비스 업체입니다. 노스럽 그루먼과 DARPA의 민관 협력으로 개발된 MRV는 두 개의 로봇 팔을 사용해 정지궤도에 있는 다른 위성에 추진 포드를 장착하고 수명을 연장합니다.)

Relativity announces new plans for Florida. Relativity Space plans to expand its operations at Cape Canaveral and add thousands of high-paying new jobs by the end of 2034, Florida Today reports . The company plans to expand test and launch support infrastructure across NASA’s Kennedy Space Center and Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, according to Space Florida, an economic development agency chartered to attract aerospace business to the state. Relativity’s plans for Florida include the construction of an additional factory for the company’s Terran R rocket, which will launch from a pad already under construction at Cape Canaveral. Relativity’s current factory is in Long Beach, California.
(상대성 이론은 플로리다에 대한 새로운 계획을 발표했습니다. 플로리다 투데이에 따르면 Relativity Space는 2034년 말까지 케이프 커내버럴에서 운영을 확장하고 수천 개의 고임금 신규 일자리를 추가할 계획입니다. 이 회사는 NASA 케네디 우주센터와 케이프 커내버럴 우주군 기지 전역에 시험 및 발사 지원 인프라를 확장할 계획이라고 경제 개발 기관인 스페이스 플로리다에 따르면, 항공우주 기업을 유치하기 위해 설립되었다. 리타티비티의 플로리다 계획에는 이미 케이프 커내버럴에서 건설 중인 발사대에서 발사될 테란 R 로켓의 추가 공장 건설이 포함되어 있다. 현재 리타티비티의 공장은 캘리포니아 롱비치에 있습니다.)

Always be scaling … “Expanding our capacity in Florida enables our ability to scale the Terran R program to support commercial, scientific, and national security missions,” said Eric Schmidt, Relativity’s executive chairman and CEO, in a statement. Officials have not announced an exact location for the Relativity rocket factory, but the company is reportedly eyeing a site in Titusville, just west of Kennedy Space Center. Relativity’s Terran R rocket, with a reusable first stage booster, remains officially scheduled for a first flight by the end of the year. That is not likely to happen.
(항상 성장해야 한다... "플로리다에서 역량을 확장함으로써 Terran R 프로그램을 상업, 과학, 국가 안보 임무를 지원할 수 있는 능력을 키울 수 있습니다."라고 Relativity의 회장 겸 CEO인 에릭 슈미트는 성명에서 말했습니다. 관계자들은 리러티비티 로켓 공장의 정확한 위치를 발표하지 않았지만, 회사는 케네디 우주센터 서쪽에 위치한 타이터스빌의 부지를 주시하고 있다고 전해졌습니다. 재사용 가능한 1단 부스터를 탑재한 Relativity의 Terran R 로켓은 연말까지 공식 첫 비행이 예정되어 있다. 그럴 가능성은 낮습니다.)

Chinese rocket overcomes lightning strike. China launched one of its most successful rockets Thursday, sending a Long March 3B launcher to orbit with a Tianlian data relay support to link Mission Control with the country’s Tiangong space station. The Long March 3B is a dependable rocket, with nearly 120 flights since entering service in 1996. But the rocket was tested on Thursday when a bolt of lightning struck the vehicle shortly after liftoff from the Xichang Satellite Launch Center in southwestern China. The rocket continued the climb into space without incident.
(중국 로켓이 번개를 극복하다. 중국은 목요일 가장 성공적인 로켓 중 하나를 발사해 창정 3B 발사체를 궤도에 올려 톈눽 데이터 중계 지원을 받아 미션 컨트롤과 국내 톈궁 우주정거장을 연결했다. 창정 3B는 신뢰할 수 있는 로켓으로, 1996년 실전 배치 이후 거의 120회의 비행을 수행했습니다. 하지만 이 로켓은 목요일에 시험되었는데, 중국 남서부 시창 위성 발사센터에서 발사 직후 번개가 차량을 강타했다. 로켓은 아무 문제 없이 우주로 상승을 계속했다.)

An occasional occurrence … It’s not every day that lightning hits a rocket during launch, but it has happened before. Most famously, lightning struck the launch of the Apollo 12 mission to the Moon in 1969, but the crew and the spacecraft persevered to complete their mission. Not all missions were so lucky. An Atlas-Centaur was destroyed by lightning during a launch from Cape Canaveral in 1987. There was no one onboard, but the incident resulted in the loss of a naval communications satellite. More recently, a Russian Soyuz rocket survived a lightning strike during a 2019 launch and delivered its payload to orbit.
(가끔 일어나는 일... 발사 중에 번개가 로켓에 맞는 일은 흔치 않지만, 이전에도 그런 일이 있었습니다. 가장 유명한 것은 1969년 아폴로 12호 달 탐사 임무 중 번개를 맞았지만, 승무원과 우주선은 임무를 완수하기 위해 끝까지 버텼습니다. 모든 임무가 그렇게 운이 좋은 것은 아니었다. 1987년 케이프 커내버럴에서 발사된 아틀라스-센타우르 항공기가 번개에 의해 파괴되었습니다. 탑승자는 없었지만, 이 사고로 해군 통신 위성 한 대가 손실되었다. 최근에는 2019년 발사 중 러시아 소유즈 로켓이 번개를 맞고 살아남아 탑재체를 궤도에 올렸습니다.)

SpaceX scrubs Starship launch attempt. SpaceX called off a test flight of its powerful Starship rocket and Super Heavy booster as the countdown clock reached zero on July 16 at the company’s spaceport in South Texas, Ars reports . Computers cut off the automated countdown sequence after some of the booster’s 33 Raptor engines didn’t light. SpaceX officials decided to move the booster off the launch pad and back to a nearby assembly building at Starbase, Texas, to swap two of its engines. The rocket returned to the launch pad this week.
(스페이스X, 스타십 발사 시도를 취소했다. Ars가 보도한 것은, 7월 16일 텍사스 남부 우주항에서 카운트다운 시계가 0에 도달하자 강력한 스타십 로켓과 슈퍼 헤비 부스터의 시험 비행을 중단했다고 전했다. 부스터의 33개 랩터 엔진 중 일부가 점화되지 않자 컴퓨터가 자동 카운트다운 시퀀스를 중단했다. 스페이스X 관계자들은 부스터를 발사대에서 텍사스 스타베이스의 인근 조립 건물로 옮겨 두 개의 엔진을 교체하기로 결정했다. 로켓은 이번 주에 발사대로 복귀했다.)

Next try Friday… Bad weather at Starbase forced SpaceX to forego a launch attempt on Thursday. The next opportunity to launch Starship will come Friday evening during a 90-minute launch window opening at 5:45 pm CDT (6:45 pm EDT; 22:45 UTC). This will be the 13th full-scale test flight of Starship and its Super Heavy booster. SpaceX aims to fly the ship halfway around the world to a controlled splashdown in the Indian Ocean. One new test objective with this launch is the deployment of 20 Starlink V3 satellites in space, the first time SpaceX has placed real spacecraft on a Starship test flight. The satellites will fly on a suborbital trajectory and burn up in the atmosphere during reentry.
(다음 시도는 금요일... 스타베이스의 악천후로 인해 스페이스X는 목요일 발사 시도를 포기해야 했다. 다음 스타십 발사 기회는 금요일 저녁 오후 5시 45분 CDT(오후 6시 45분 EDT; 22:45 UTC)에 열리는 90분 발사 창 중 찾아올 예정입니다. 이번이 스타쉽과 슈퍼 헤비 부스터의 13번째 본격 시험 비행이 될 것입니다. 스페이스X는 우주선을 지구 반대편까지 인도양에서 통제된 착수(controlled splashdown)를 목표로 하고 있습니다. 이번 발사의 새로운 시험 목표 중 하나는 20기의 스타링크 V3 위성을 우주에 배치하는 것으로, 이는 스페이스X가 실제 우주선을 스타쉽 시험 비행에 처음 배치한 사례입니다. 위성들은 준궤도 궤도를 따라 비행하며 재진입 시 대기권에서 소각됩니다.)

Artemis III is getting more real. Stacking of the Space Launch System rocket for the Artemis III mission is underway at Kennedy Space Center in Florida, NASA reports . The monthslong stacking sequence began with the placement of the lower segments of the rocket’s solid-fueled boosters on the Mobile Launcher inside the Vehicle Assembly Building (VAB). Ground teams will stack the five-segment boosters in the coming weeks, then lower the core stage between the boosters. That will be followed by the installation of a “spacer” structure on top of the core stage to connect it with the Orion spacecraft, which will carry a crew of four astronauts to low-Earth orbit to rendezvous with prototypes of commercial Moon landers developed by SpaceX and Blue Origin.
(아르테미스 III는 점점 더 현실감 있게 변하고 있습니다. NASA가 보도한 바에 따르면, 아르테미스 III 임무를 위한 우주발사시스템 로켓의 스택이 플로리다 케네디 우주센터에서 진행 중입니다. 수개월에 걸친 적재 과정은 로켓의 고체 연료 부스터 하단 구간을 차량 조립 건물(VAB) 내 이동식 발사기에 배치하는 것으로 시작되었다. 지상팀은 앞으로 몇 주 내에 5세그먼트 부스터를 쌓고, 부스터 사이에 코어 단계를 낮출 예정입니다. 이어 코어 스테이지 상단에 '스페이서' 구조물이 설치되어 오리온 우주선과 연결될 예정이며, 이 우주선은 4명의 우주비행사를 저지구 궤도에 태워 스페이스X와 블루 오리진이 개발한 상업용 달 착륙선 프로토타입과 랑데부할 예정입니다.)

Core stage status… Workers are completing the integration of the SLS core stage itself elsewhere in the VAB. The main structure of the core stage arrived at Kennedy in April from a factory in New Orleans. Since then, ground teams have connected the engine section to the bottom of the core stage. The next step will be the installation of the core stage’s four RS-25 main engines. NASA officials would like to complete the initial stacking of the SLS rocket for Artemis III, without the Orion spacecraft, in time to begin fueling tests at the launch pad by the end of the year.
(핵심 무대 상태... 작업자들은 VAB 내 다른 곳에서 SLS 코어 단계 자체의 통합을 완료하고 있습니다. 핵심 단계의 주요 구조물은 4월에 뉴올리언스의 한 공장에서 케네디에 도착했다. 그 이후로 지상 팀은 엔진 부분을 코어 단계 하단에 연결했습니다. 다음 단계는 코어 스테이지의 4개 RS-25 주 엔진 설치입니다. NASA 관계자들은 오리온 우주선 없이 아르테미스 III용 SLS 로켓의 초기 스택을 완료하여 올해 말까지 발사대에서 연료 주입 테스트를 시작할 수 있기를 원한다.)

July 24: Starship | Flight 13 | Starbase, Texas | 22:45 UTC
(7월 24일: 스타쉽 | 13편 | 스타베이스, 텍사스 | 22:45 UTC)

July 25: Falcon 9 | Starlink 17-51 | Vandenberg Space Force Base, California | 14:00 UTC
(7월 25일: 팔콘 9 | 스타링크 17-51 | 캘리포니아 밴덴버그 우주군 기지 | 14:00 UTC)

July 29: Falcon 9 | Starlink 17-52 | Vandenberg Space Force Base, California | 02:00 UTC
(7월 29일: 팔콘 9 | 스타링크 17-52 | 캘리포니아 밴덴버그 우주군 기지 | 02:00 UTC)

item.title: This is the world’s most advanced robotic servicing satellite—that we know about (This is the world’s most advanced robotic servicing satellite—that we know about)
item.description:
“These are things that tend to be really hard.”
(“These are things that tend to be really hard.”)

A spacecraft fitted with two flexible robotic arms is on the way to geosynchronous orbit after launching earlier this week on a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket, kicking off a planned decade-long mission to open new frontiers in satellite servicing.
(A spacecraft fitted with two flexible robotic arms is on the way to geosynchronous orbit after launching earlier this week on a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket, kicking off a planned decade-long mission to open new frontiers in satellite servicing.)

The Mission Robotic Vehicle, owned and built by Northrop Grumman, rocketed into orbit from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida on Tuesday. Three small propulsion pods, each functioning as standalone spacecraft, accompanied the MRV aboard the Falcon 9 rocket.
(The Mission Robotic Vehicle, owned and built by Northrop Grumman, rocketed into orbit from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida on Tuesday. Three small propulsion pods, each functioning as standalone spacecraft, accompanied the MRV aboard the Falcon 9 rocket.)

The Falcon 9 deployed all four payloads within about an hour of liftoff. It will take about a year for the satellites to maneuver from their initial elliptical drop-off orbit into a circular orbit more than 22,000 miles (nearly 36,000 kilometers) over the equator. At this altitude, the MRV and the three Mission Extension Pods (MEPs) will travel in lockstep with Earth’s rotation, operating in the same kind of orbit as numerous civilian and military communications satellites, missile warning platforms, and a growing number of spy satellites.
(The Falcon 9 deployed all four payloads within about an hour of liftoff. It will take about a year for the satellites to maneuver from their initial elliptical drop-off orbit into a circular orbit more than 22,000 miles (nearly 36,000 kilometers) over the equator. At this altitude, the MRV and the three Mission Extension Pods (MEPs) will travel in lockstep with Earth’s rotation, operating in the same kind of orbit as numerous civilian and military communications satellites, missile warning platforms, and a growing number of spy satellites.)

That’s when the real fun will begin.
(That’s when the real fun will begin.)

The Mission Robotic Vehicle is arguably the most advanced servicing satellite ever launched. It’s certainly the most sophisticated orbiting servicer we know anything about. China launched a satellite with a robotic arm into geosynchronous orbit in 2016. Another launch in 2021 deployed the Shijian-21 or SJ-21, spacecraft on a “space debris mitigation” mission. SJ-21 linked up with a defunct Chinese navigation satellite and moved it to a higher altitude for disposal before returning to the geosynchronous belt.
(The Mission Robotic Vehicle is arguably the most advanced servicing satellite ever launched. It’s certainly the most sophisticated orbiting servicer we know anything about. China launched a satellite with a robotic arm into geosynchronous orbit in 2016. Another launch in 2021 deployed the Shijian-21 or SJ-21, spacecraft on a “space debris mitigation” mission. SJ-21 linked up with a defunct Chinese navigation satellite and moved it to a higher altitude for disposal before returning to the geosynchronous belt.)

China launched the SJ-25 refueling mission in January 2025, and it docked with SJ-21 a few months later before the satellites went their separate ways, completing what was apparently the first refueling demonstration so far from Earth. The extra gas is expected to give SJ-21 a longer life, giving it the potential to visit and reposition other satellites in geosynchronous orbit.
(China launched the SJ-25 refueling mission in January 2025, and it docked with SJ-21 a few months later before the satellites went their separate ways, completing what was apparently the first refueling demonstration so far from Earth. The extra gas is expected to give SJ-21 a longer life, giving it the potential to visit and reposition other satellites in geosynchronous orbit.)

Northrop Grumman and its subsidiary, SpaceLogistics, have the same idea with the Mission Robotic Vehicle. There are clear military applications for this capability. Last year, the head of US Space Command, Gen. Stephen Whiting, told Congress that China was developing “on-orbit, maneuverable counterspace satellites to target our satellites using dual-use technologies.” He explicitly called out SJ-21 as an example of a mission that China could use “for potential offensive purposes against satellites we rely on to defend the homeland and project power.”
(Northrop Grumman and its subsidiary, SpaceLogistics, have the same idea with the Mission Robotic Vehicle. There are clear military applications for this capability. Last year, the head of US Space Command, Gen. Stephen Whiting, told Congress that China was developing “on-orbit, maneuverable counterspace satellites to target our satellites using dual-use technologies.” He explicitly called out SJ-21 as an example of a mission that China could use “for potential offensive purposes against satellites we rely on to defend the homeland and project power.”)

The US Space Force already has a fleet of inspector satellites roaming geosynchronous orbit to observe and report on the activities of foreign spacecraft. US military operators maneuvered one of these inspector satellites near the SJ-21 and SJ-25 satellites during the refueling operation last year.
(The US Space Force already has a fleet of inspector satellites roaming geosynchronous orbit to observe and report on the activities of foreign spacecraft. US military operators maneuvered one of these inspector satellites near the SJ-21 and SJ-25 satellites during the refueling operation last year.)

But military officials hadn’t publicly acknowledged any US-owned satellite with capabilities similar to China’s trio of Shijian satellites. That changes with Northrop Grumman’s MRV mission. The Pentagon’s Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) spent approximately $420 million to develop the satellite’s robotics payload, alongside hundreds of millions of dollars invested by Northrop Grumman.
(But military officials hadn’t publicly acknowledged any US-owned satellite with capabilities similar to China’s trio of Shijian satellites. That changes with Northrop Grumman’s MRV mission. The Pentagon’s Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) spent approximately $420 million to develop the satellite’s robotics payload, alongside hundreds of millions of dollars invested by Northrop Grumman.)

The public-private partnership brought Northrop Grumman’s preexisting commercial satellite servicing program together with DARPA’s Robotic Servicing of Geosynchronous Satellites (RSGS) program. These programs originally operated independently.
(The public-private partnership brought Northrop Grumman’s preexisting commercial satellite servicing program together with DARPA’s Robotic Servicing of Geosynchronous Satellites (RSGS) program. These programs originally operated independently.)

Northrop Grumman developed two satellites called Mission Extension Vehicles and launched them in 2019 and 2020. The MEVs docked with aging commercial communications satellites in geosynchronous orbit to take over pointing and orbit control. The MRV builds on the MEV concept, but thanks to the DARPA-funded robotic arms, the new servicer doesn’t have to commit itself to a single client. It can use the arms to install Northrop’s Mission Extension Pods on multiple geosynchronous satellites.=
(Northrop Grumman developed two satellites called Mission Extension Vehicles and launched them in 2019 and 2020. The MEVs docked with aging commercial communications satellites in geosynchronous orbit to take over pointing and orbit control. The MRV builds on the MEV concept, but thanks to the DARPA-funded robotic arms, the new servicer doesn’t have to commit itself to a single client. It can use the arms to install Northrop’s Mission Extension Pods on multiple geosynchronous satellites.=)

This isn’t refueling, but the MRV serves the same end. The Space Force has a separate contract with a company named Astroscale to demonstrate refueling in geosynchronous orbit next year, something no US company has done before. The MRV can also do more than life extension. It can inspect, service, upgrade, or repair satellites that were never designed for it.
(This isn’t refueling, but the MRV serves the same end. The Space Force has a separate contract with a company named Astroscale to demonstrate refueling in geosynchronous orbit next year, something no US company has done before. The MRV can also do more than life extension. It can inspect, service, upgrade, or repair satellites that were never designed for it.)

DARPA partnered with the Naval Research Laboratory to develop the RSGS robotics payload. More than 20 years in the making, the robotics system was designed to meet Defense Department reliability standards, including redundant robotic arms, avionics, and mission troops. The RSGS payload also features cameras and sensors to allow the MRV to autonomously approach, inspect, capture, and upgrade client satellites that weren’t designed for visitors.
(DARPA partnered with the Naval Research Laboratory to develop the RSGS robotics payload. More than 20 years in the making, the robotics system was designed to meet Defense Department reliability standards, including redundant robotic arms, avionics, and mission troops. The RSGS payload also features cameras and sensors to allow the MRV to autonomously approach, inspect, capture, and upgrade client satellites that weren’t designed for visitors.)

“This journey to the launch pad represents the culmination of a multiple decades-long endeavor of vision, risk, and relentless engineering,” Bernard Kelm, acting director of NRL’s Naval Center for Space Technology, said in a statement. DARPA first funded NRL’s space robotics work in 2002, a small study for a concept called RescueSat . RSGS can trace its lineage back to that initiative.
(“This journey to the launch pad represents the culmination of a multiple decades-long endeavor of vision, risk, and relentless engineering,” Bernard Kelm, acting director of NRL’s Naval Center for Space Technology, said in a statement. DARPA first funded NRL’s space robotics work in 2002, a small study for a concept called RescueSat . RSGS can trace its lineage back to that initiative.)

“RSGS is designed to permanently change this ‘launch-and-abandon’ archetype,” Kelm said. “The RSGS program shifts this paradigm by enabling on-orbit interventions, including inspections, mechanical anomaly resolution, satellite relocation and upgrades.”
(“RSGS is designed to permanently change this ‘launch-and-abandon’ archetype,” Kelm said. “The RSGS program shifts this paradigm by enabling on-orbit interventions, including inspections, mechanical anomaly resolution, satellite relocation and upgrades.”)

﻿
(﻿)

This isn’t DARPA’s first foray into satellite servicing. The agency’s Orbital Express mission , launched in 2007, completed several months of rendezvous and docking maneuvers, robotic arm tests, and other servicing demonstrations in low-Earth orbit. DARPA formally established the RSGS program in 2015, building on the robotics work already underway at the Naval Research Laboratory. DARPA initially selected Maxar— now Lanteris Space Systems —to partner on the RSGS program, but the company backed out, and DARPA replaced Maxar with Northrop Grumman in 2020.
(This isn’t DARPA’s first foray into satellite servicing. The agency’s Orbital Express mission , launched in 2007, completed several months of rendezvous and docking maneuvers, robotic arm tests, and other servicing demonstrations in low-Earth orbit. DARPA formally established the RSGS program in 2015, building on the robotics work already underway at the Naval Research Laboratory. DARPA initially selected Maxar— now Lanteris Space Systems —to partner on the RSGS program, but the company backed out, and DARPA replaced Maxar with Northrop Grumman in 2020.)

NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center also contributed its engineering expertise to the RSGS program after NASA canceled its own robotic satellite servicing mission in 2024. NASA’s support included the development of dynamic simulation and analysis tools, software verification, and a team of flight robot operators to assist ground controllers during mission operations.
(NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center also contributed its engineering expertise to the RSGS program after NASA canceled its own robotic satellite servicing mission in 2024. NASA’s support included the development of dynamic simulation and analysis tools, software verification, and a team of flight robot operators to assist ground controllers during mission operations.)

“RSGS is designed to work on satellites that haven’t been prepared, and as a result, it has more complex robotics,” said Jim Shoemaker, RSGS program manager at DARPA. “This was designed as an operational system. Orbital Express had one arm. RSGS has two arms, which is good. It gives you more capability. Plus, it gives you some redundancy if you have an issue with one of the arms during the mission. The other difference here is DARPA is working to transition the capability to industry, so this is a private-public partnership.”
(“RSGS is designed to work on satellites that haven’t been prepared, and as a result, it has more complex robotics,” said Jim Shoemaker, RSGS program manager at DARPA. “This was designed as an operational system. Orbital Express had one arm. RSGS has two arms, which is good. It gives you more capability. Plus, it gives you some redundancy if you have an issue with one of the arms during the mission. The other difference here is DARPA is working to transition the capability to industry, so this is a private-public partnership.”)

Northrop Grumman’s first three Mission Extension Pods launched on the same rocket as the MRV, but they are flying separately up to geosynchronous orbit using electric propulsion. The pods, each about the size of a dishwasher unit, will loiter there for retrieval by the MRV’s robotic arms. After picking up the first pod, the servicing spacecraft will rendezvous with its first client satellite, lining up precisely with the client to install the pod into its engine compartment. The MEP will latch onto the satellite and take over propulsion for up to eight years, acting as a jetpack, or a smaller version of the MEV, to move the client around geosynchronous orbit as needed.
(Northrop Grumman’s first three Mission Extension Pods launched on the same rocket as the MRV, but they are flying separately up to geosynchronous orbit using electric propulsion. The pods, each about the size of a dishwasher unit, will loiter there for retrieval by the MRV’s robotic arms. After picking up the first pod, the servicing spacecraft will rendezvous with its first client satellite, lining up precisely with the client to install the pod into its engine compartment. The MEP will latch onto the satellite and take over propulsion for up to eight years, acting as a jetpack, or a smaller version of the MEV, to move the client around geosynchronous orbit as needed.)

“You can’t fly this with a joystick from the ground because the time delay is too long,” Shoemaker told Ars. “You have to be able to either upload a mission script or let the satellite execute it on its own.”
(“You can’t fly this with a joystick from the ground because the time delay is too long,” Shoemaker told Ars. “You have to be able to either upload a mission script or let the satellite execute it on its own.”)

Engineers extensively tested the robotic arms on the ground, in the full measure of Earth’s gravity. Things will work differently in microgravity.
(Engineers extensively tested the robotic arms on the ground, in the full measure of Earth’s gravity. Things will work differently in microgravity.)

“Inertia operates differently in space,” Shoemaker said. “When you move the arm one direction, the entire satellite wants to rotate the opposite direction, so every motion of the arms has to be compensated by the control system to keep the satellite in the same position, which is fairly complicated.”
(“Inertia operates differently in space,” Shoemaker said. “When you move the arm one direction, the entire satellite wants to rotate the opposite direction, so every motion of the arms has to be compensated by the control system to keep the satellite in the same position, which is fairly complicated.”)

“And then, when you attach yourself to another satellite, you change the dynamics completely because you’ve doubled the mass and the dimensions, and so your control system has to be able to adapt to that new configuration,” he continued. “These are things that tend to be really hard.”
(“And then, when you attach yourself to another satellite, you change the dynamics completely because you’ve doubled the mass and the dimensions, and so your control system has to be able to adapt to that new configuration,” he continued. “These are things that tend to be really hard.”)

The robotic arms can do more than manipulate Northrop’s propulsion modules. The hands of the arms can accommodate different types of tools. The mission launched this week with two pod capture tools used for grappling the MEPs or any other object with a grapple fixture. The MRV also has two copies of a “Marman ring” tool that will allow the main servicing spacecraft to directly grab onto a client satellite if required.
(The robotic arms can do more than manipulate Northrop’s propulsion modules. The hands of the arms can accommodate different types of tools. The mission launched this week with two pod capture tools used for grappling the MEPs or any other object with a grapple fixture. The MRV also has two copies of a “Marman ring” tool that will allow the main servicing spacecraft to directly grab onto a client satellite if required.)

Northrop Grumman and SpaceLogistics have not identified which satellite will be the first stop for the MRV. The companies have commercial agreements with two communications satellite operators, SES and Optus, to add jetpacks to their spacecraft using the MRV. The Space Force is also expected to use the MRV to visit at least one of its satellites.
(Northrop Grumman and SpaceLogistics have not identified which satellite will be the first stop for the MRV. The companies have commercial agreements with two communications satellite operators, SES and Optus, to add jetpacks to their spacecraft using the MRV. The Space Force is also expected to use the MRV to visit at least one of its satellites.)

Northrop Grumman took ownership of the government-funded robotics payload at launch, but the company still owes DARPA information about the performance of the mission through the first servicing call.
(Northrop Grumman took ownership of the government-funded robotics payload at launch, but the company still owes DARPA information about the performance of the mission through the first servicing call.)

“After they finish that demonstration, DARPA, the government, is sort of out of the driver’s seat because that’s when we really hand things over,” Shoemaker said.
(“After they finish that demonstration, DARPA, the government, is sort of out of the driver’s seat because that’s when we really hand things over,” Shoemaker said.)

The Space Force will then take over DARPA’s role as the government partner. Northrop Grumman will retain ownership of the satellite and the payload and will remain responsible for day-to-day operations.
(The Space Force will then take over DARPA’s role as the government partner. Northrop Grumman will retain ownership of the satellite and the payload and will remain responsible for day-to-day operations.)

“They’ll operate it for 10 to 13 years, which is the mean mission lifetime,” Shoemaker said. “So the US government benefits from getting the servicing capability on orbit without having to pay the long-term care and feeding. As needed, the US government can contract with Northrop Grumman to get services.”
(“They’ll operate it for 10 to 13 years, which is the mean mission lifetime,” Shoemaker said. “So the US government benefits from getting the servicing capability on orbit without having to pay the long-term care and feeding. As needed, the US government can contract with Northrop Grumman to get services.”)

Mission managers emphasized the MRV’s adaptability in interviews with Ars. This is what sets it apart from other satellite servicing missions , Shoemaker said.
(Mission managers emphasized the MRV’s adaptability in interviews with Ars. This is what sets it apart from other satellite servicing missions , Shoemaker said.)

“RSGS has full seven-degree-of-freedom robotic arms, heavily instrumented. The ends of the arms can attach multiple tools as hands, and they also have a good deal of autonomous control,” Shoemaker said. “It’s general-purpose, high-dexterity robotics.”
(“RSGS has full seven-degree-of-freedom robotic arms, heavily instrumented. The ends of the arms can attach multiple tools as hands, and they also have a good deal of autonomous control,” Shoemaker said. “It’s general-purpose, high-dexterity robotics.”)

Ground teams could build and launch more jetpacks to meet up with the MRV in geosynchronous orbit after the spacecraft uses the three pods already in space. Future launches could carry new tools, such as a knife, a cutter, or a robotic screwdriver for more invasive servicing or repairs. And the MRV itself is designed to be refueled in orbit. Northrop Grumman doesn’t plan to immediately build a second MRV, but it will continue upgrading and augmenting the vehicle it just launched.
(Ground teams could build and launch more jetpacks to meet up with the MRV in geosynchronous orbit after the spacecraft uses the three pods already in space. Future launches could carry new tools, such as a knife, a cutter, or a robotic screwdriver for more invasive servicing or repairs. And the MRV itself is designed to be refueled in orbit. Northrop Grumman doesn’t plan to immediately build a second MRV, but it will continue upgrading and augmenting the vehicle it just launched.)

Another idea is to use the MRV to enable a new era in orbital logistics, not just servicing and life extension. The spacecraft could theoretically be part of a logistics train in geosynchronous orbit. A depot spacecraft, such as Northrop’s own ROOSTER satellite platform or Blue Origin’s Blue Ring , could launch with a cache of prepositioned spare parts, payloads, and sensors. The MRV could come pick up these payloads and take them to the satellites that need them.
(Another idea is to use the MRV to enable a new era in orbital logistics, not just servicing and life extension. The spacecraft could theoretically be part of a logistics train in geosynchronous orbit. A depot spacecraft, such as Northrop’s own ROOSTER satellite platform or Blue Origin’s Blue Ring , could launch with a cache of prepositioned spare parts, payloads, and sensors. The MRV could come pick up these payloads and take them to the satellites that need them.)

The most lucrative national security market for satellite servicing is, at first, likely to be in geosynchronous orbit, home to some of the military’s most expensive multibillion-dollar satellites. The spacecraft there are one-of-a-kind or operate in small fleets. Despite the distance from Earth, this makes geosynchronous satellites vulnerable to attack. Satellites in low-Earth orbit, just a few hundred miles above the planet, are often (but not always) part of large proliferated constellations such as SpaceX’s Starlink. With a few exceptions, military and commercial satellites in LEO are less expensive and easier to replace than satellites in GEO.
(The most lucrative national security market for satellite servicing is, at first, likely to be in geosynchronous orbit, home to some of the military’s most expensive multibillion-dollar satellites. The spacecraft there are one-of-a-kind or operate in small fleets. Despite the distance from Earth, this makes geosynchronous satellites vulnerable to attack. Satellites in low-Earth orbit, just a few hundred miles above the planet, are often (but not always) part of large proliferated constellations such as SpaceX’s Starlink. With a few exceptions, military and commercial satellites in LEO are less expensive and easier to replace than satellites in GEO.)

But there’s a future for refueling and servicing in LEO. NASA signed a contract last year with Katalyst Space Technologies, a satellite manufacturing startup, to reboost one of its astronomy satellites in LEO. Katalyst launched the mission last month, and the spacecraft is now in pursuit of its client.
(But there’s a future for refueling and servicing in LEO. NASA signed a contract last year with Katalyst Space Technologies, a satellite manufacturing startup, to reboost one of its astronomy satellites in LEO. Katalyst launched the mission last month, and the spacecraft is now in pursuit of its client.)

SpaceX is planning the most ambitious refueling demonstration in history with its Starship rocket. SpaceX aims to transfer cryogenic propellants between Starships in LEO, perhaps late this year or next year, in a precursor experiment for future large-scale refueling sorties to support Moon landings for NASA’s Artemis program.
(SpaceX is planning the most ambitious refueling demonstration in history with its Starship rocket. SpaceX aims to transfer cryogenic propellants between Starships in LEO, perhaps late this year or next year, in a precursor experiment for future large-scale refueling sorties to support Moon landings for NASA’s Artemis program.)

These companies and more are taking distinct paths toward satellite servicing, orbital refueling, in-space depots, and what the military likes to call dynamic space operations . But the trend is unmistakable: to fully utilize the domain of space, the throwaway mentality must go.

item.title: Team uses AlphaFold AI to redesign gene-editing proteins to make them safer (팀은 알파폴드 AI를 사용해 유전자 편집 단백질을 더 안전하게 재설계합니다)
item.description:
Google’s AlphaFold can help ID what parts of a gene editing protein enable mistakes.
(구글의 AlphaFold는 유전자 편집 단백질의 어떤 부분이 실수를 유발하는지 식별하는 데 도움을 줄 수 있습니다.)

A couple of decades after the discovery of systems that could selectively target DNA, we’re starting to see the first therapies based on gene editing. One challenge these developments have faced is safety. While we can make them pretty specific to the gene we want edited, the human genome is very large, and even rare DNA sequences can appear a couple of times by chance.
(DNA를 선택적으로 표적으로 할 수 있는 시스템이 발견된 지 수십 년이 지난 지금, 우리는 유전자 편집에 기반한 최초의 치료법을 보기 시작했습니다. 이러한 발전이 직면한 한 가지 도전 과제는 안전입니다. 우리가 편집하고자 하는 유전자에 꽤 특이적으로 만들 수는 있지만, 인간 게놈은 매우 크고, 희귀한 DNA 서열도 우연히 몇 번 나타날 수 있습니다.)

As a result, all the original gene-editing systems had known rates of what are called off-target effects, in which they simply edit the wrong sequence. This may be a low-probability event, but edit enough cells—and therapies generally have to edit many—and errors become inevitable.
(그 결과, 모든 원래 유전자 편집 시스템은 잘못된 서열을 편집하는 '오프타겟 효과'의 비율이 알려져 있었습니다. 이것은 확률이 낮을 수 있지만, 충분한 셀을 편집하면—치료법은 일반적으로 많은 셀을 편집해야 하므로—오류가 불가피해집니다.)

A lot of effort has gone into finding ways to minimize or eliminate off-target edits. In a recent issue of Nature, researchers described modifying the AI protein-folding software AlphaFold to help identify key areas of gene-editing proteins responsible for off-target effects. Those areas were then modified to reduce the problems.
(빗나간 편집을 최소화하거나 제거하는 방법을 찾는 데 많은 노력이 들어갔습니다. 최근 네이처지(Nature) 호에서 연구자들은 AI 단백질 접힘 소프트웨어인 알파폴드(AlphaFold)를 수정하여 오프타겟 효과를 일으키는 유전자 편집 단백질의 핵심 영역을 파악하는 방법을 설명했습니다. 그 지역들은 문제를 줄이기 위해 개조되었습니다.)

Gene-editing systems have three key components. The first is guide RNA, which can base-pair with the targeted genome sequence. It’s possible to design many guide RNAs that all target the same gene, so one approach to making the system safer is to pick sequences that don’t share much similarity with any other genomic locations. This is now widely used as part of the basic design process for a gene-editing system.
(유전자 편집 시스템은 세 가지 핵심 구성 요소로 이루어져 있습니다. 첫 번째는 표적 유전체 서열과 염기쌍을 형성할 수 있는 가이드 RNA입니다. 동일한 유전자를 표적으로 하는 여러 가이드 RNA를 설계할 수 있기 때문에, 시스템을 더 안전하게 만드는 한 가지 방법은 다른 유전체 위치와 크게 닮지 않은 서열을 선택하는 것입니다. 이 방법은 현재 유전자 편집 시스템의 기본 설계 과정의 일부로 널리 사용되고 있습니다.)

The second component is a Cas protein named after the CRISPR system’s Cas9 protein. It interacts with both the guide RNA and genomic RNA and helps enforce the specificity of the interactions.
(두 번째 성분은 CRISPR 시스템의 Cas9 단백질에서 이름을 딴 Cas 단백질입니다. 이 과정은 가이드 RNA와 유전체 RNA 모두와 상호작용하며 상호작용의 특이성을 강화하는 데 도움을 줍니다.)

If there are too many mismatches in the base pairing between the RNA and DNA, Cas9 (or other Cas family members) won’t stick there. Various approaches have led to improved Cas family members that have reduced the tendency to enable off-target edits.
(RNA와 DNA 사이의 염기쌍이 너무 많이 불일치하면 Cas9(또는 다른 Cas 계열 구성원)가 그 자리에 머무르지 않습니다. 다양한 접근법 덕분에 Cas 계열 구성원이 개선되어 빗나간 편집 경향이 줄어들었습니다.)

The final key component of the system is the protein that interacts with Cas9 when it’s bound to DNA and modifies the DNA. In the original CRISPR system, this cut both strands of the double helix, producing damage that’s difficult to control. Researchers have since modified other proteins to interact with Cas9 but catalyze more subtle changes to DNA, such as lopping off a single base or making chemical modifications that alter how it base-pairs.
(시스템의 마지막 핵심 구성 요소는 Cas9이 DNA에 결합했을 때 상호작용하여 DNA를 변형하는 단백질입니다. 원래 CRISPR 시스템에서는 이중 나선의 양쪽 가닥을 모두 절단하여 통제하기 어려운 손상을 발생시켰습니다. 이후 연구자들은 다른 단백질들을 변형하여 Cas9과 상호작용하도록 했으며, 단일 염기를 절단하거나 염기쌍 형성 방식을 바꾸는 화학적 변형을 통해 DNA에 더 미묘한 변화를 촉매하는 방식을 시도했습니다.)

Overall, the length of the base pairing between the guide RNAs and the genome is on the order of 18 bases long. That should show up in random DNA sequences only about once in 70 billion bases, and our genome is only about 3 billion bases. By that measure, we should be good. But it turns out that Cas9 can tolerate a small number of mispaired bases without losing its ability to stick to DNA. The exact number and location of the bases where variations are tolerated can vary somewhat, making it difficult to identify in advance which guide RNAs might pose a danger.
(전반적으로 가이드 RNA와 게놈 사이의 염기쌍 길이는 약 18염기입니다. 이 염기는 무작위 DNA 서열에서 700억 염기당 한 번 정도만 나타나야 하며, 우리 게놈은 약 30억 염기입니다. 그 기준으로 보면 괜찮을 거야. 하지만 Cas9은 소수의 불쌍 염기를 견디면서도 DNA에 붙는 능력을 잃지 않는다는 것이 밝혀졌습니다. 변이가 허용되는 염기의 정확한 수와 위치는 다소 달라져, 어떤 가이드 RNA가 위험할 수 있는지 사전에 파악하기 어렵습니다.)

One route to improving safety is to better understand how these off-target interactions occur.
(안전성을 높이는 한 가지 방법은 이러한 비표적 상호작용이 어떻게 발생하는지 더 잘 이해하는 것입니다.)

The team behind the new work, based at a variety of institutions in China, reasoned out their approach in advance. A perfectly matched DNA-RNA hybrid will have one structure, while one with one or more mispaired bases will have a slightly different structure. Evolution has optimized the structure of the Cas9 to stick to the former. But it apparently hasn’t prevented Cas9 from adopting slightly different conformations that can interact with mispaired structures.
(중국 내 여러 기관에 기반을 둔 이 새로운 연구팀이 사전에 접근법을 논리적으로 정했습니다. 완벽하게 일치하는 DNA-RNA 하이브리드는 하나의 구조를 가지지만, 하나 이상의 염기가 불쌍한 경우에는 약간 다른 구조를 가집니다. 진화는 Cas9의 구조를 전자에 맞게 최적화했습니다. 하지만 Cas9이 불쌍한 구조와 상호작용할 수 있는 약간 다른 구조를 채택하는 것을 막지는 못한 것으로 보입니다.)

If we can identify the portions of Cas9 that mediate these problematic interactions, we can modify and potentially block them.
(이러한 문제적 상호작용을 매개하는 Cas9 부분을 식별할 수 있다면, 이를 수정하고 잠재적으로 차단할 수 있습니다.)

The team’s first step was to build a large library of off-target editing sites. They did this by using a modified CRISPR system that converts the DNA base adenine to a related chemical, inosine, and then isolating any DNA fragments that contain it. They repeated this process with 10 different guide RNAs and analyzed a large number of modified DNA fragments from each to get a broad picture of the types of off-target sequences present.
(팀의 첫 번째 단계는 빗나간 편집 사이트들의 대규모 라이브러리를 구축하는 것이었습니다. 이들은 수정된 CRISPR 시스템을 사용해 DNA 염기물 아데닌을 관련 화학물질인 이노신으로 전환하고, 이를 포함하는 DNA 조각을 분리하는 방식으로 이 작업을 진행했습니다. 이 과정을 10개의 서로 다른 가이드 RNA로 반복하고, 각 RNA에서 다수의 변형된 DNA 조각을 분석하여 오프타겟 서열의 유형을 폭넓게 파악했습니다.)

The next step was to examine how the CRISPR complex interacted with them, using the AlphaFold AI-based protein-folding software. Updated versions were designed to handle interactions between proteins and nucleic acids , as well as complexes of multiple proteins. So the team fed AlphaFold versions of a target DNA sequence, along with a guide RNA, the Cas9 sequence, and an enzyme that chemically modifies bases and can stick to Cas9.
(다음 단계는 AlphaFold AI 기반 단백질 접기 소프트웨어를 사용해 CRISPR 복합체가 이들과 어떻게 상호작용하는지 조사하는 것이었습니다. 업데이트된 버전은 단백질과 핵산 간 상호작용뿐만 아니라 여러 단백질의 복합체도 처리할 수 있도록 설계되었습니다. 그래서 연구팀은 표적 DNA 서열의 알파폴드 버전과 가이드 RNA, Cas9 서열, 그리고 염기를 화학적으로 변형하고 Cas9에 달라붙는 효소를 함께 먹였다.)

Unfortunately, it choked, placing one of the proteins in what was clearly the wrong location.
(불행히도 그 음식이 질식해 단백질 하나를 분명히 잘못된 위치에 넣었다.)

Undeterred, the team simplified things and fed AlphaFold only the DNA, RNA, and Cas9 protein, since the latter is the primary factor determining its sequence specificity. This worked much better, producing a structure that agreed with ones determined by experiments with actual nucleic acids and proteins.
(그러나 굴하지 않고 연구팀은 단순화하여 알파폴드에 DNA, RNA, Cas9 단백질만 공급했는데, Cas9가 서열 특이성을 결정하는 주요 요인이기 때문입니다. 이 방법은 훨씬 더 잘 작동하여 실제 핵산과 단백질을 이용한 실험으로 결정된 구조와 일치하는 구조를 만들어냈다.)

By comparing the structures AlphaFold generated when fed different on- and off-target sites, the researchers found a general pattern. Many (about two-thirds) of the off-target sites caused the Cas9 protein to adopt a slightly different structure. But nearly all (over 95 percent) of them altered which amino acids contacted the RNA. So there are clearly some cases where Cas9 maintains its normal structure but amino acids within it flex around in ways that accommodate the mispaired bases of off-target sites.
(연구진은 알파폴드가 서로 다른 온타겟 및 오프타겟 부위에 공급될 때 생성되는 구조를 비교하여 일반적인 패턴을 발견했습니다. 약 3분의 2의 오프타깃 부위가 Cas9 단백질에 약간 다른 구조를 갖게 했습니다. 하지만 거의 모든 연구(95% 이상)가 RNA와 접촉하는 아미노산을 변경했습니다. 따라서 Cas9이 정상 구조를 유지하면서도 그 안의 아미노산이 불쌍한 염기의 불균형을 수용하도록 유연한 경우도 분명히 존재합니다.)

Conveniently, AlphaFold was already set up to identify what is termed the “contact probability,” namely, the chance that any two items, such as amino acids or nucleotides, are within a very small distance (eight Angstroms). The researchers could take the output of the contact probability analysis for on- and off-target sites and compare them, identifying exactly which amino acids in Cas9 have altered contacts when there’s a mismatch between the guide RNA and the DNA. They termed this computerized analysis setup “ContactSeek.”
(편리하게도 알파폴드는 이미 '접촉 확률'이라 불리는 것을 식별하도록 설정되어 있었는데, 이는 아미노산이나 뉴클레오타이드 같은 두 항목이 매우 짧은 거리(8 앙스트롬) 내에 있을 확률입니다. 연구진은 온타겟 및 오프타겟 부위의 접촉 확률 분석 결과를 비교하여 가이드 RNA와 DNA 간의 불일치 시 Cas9 내 어떤 아미노산이 접촉이 변하는지 정확히 식별할 수 있습니다. 이 컴퓨터 분석 시스템을 "ContactSeek"이라고 명명했습니다.)

On its own, ContactSeek tended to produce a large list of amino acids that shift around when bound to an off-target site. So the researchers focused on regions of the Cas9 protein where these amino acids clustered, viewing this as a sign that these areas were adapting to the differences caused by mismatched bases. They then began to test versions of Cas9 with different amino acids at these sites.
(ContactSeek은 단독으로 오프타겟 부위에 결합되면 이동하는 아미노산의 방대한 목록을 생성하는 경향이 있었습니다. 그래서 연구진은 이 아미노산들이 모인 Cas9 단백질 영역에 집중하며, 이 부위들이 불일치하는 염기로 인한 차이에 적응하고 있다는 신호로 보았습니다. 그 후 이들 부위에서 다양한 아미노산을 사용한 Cas9 버전을 시험하기 시작했습니다.)

In all, the researchers made 23 different swaps, putting a different amino acid into one of 10 key positions identified by their work with AlphaFold. This allowed them to find a variant with activity similar to the normal Cas9 at sites that matched the target sequence, while its off-target activity dropped from 28 percent to 5 percent. Similar results were possible when the researchers used different guide RNAs. They also showed that the approach worked for a similar system that used a different Cas protein (Cas12) to recognize the DNA/guide RNA combination.
(총 23번의 서로 다른 아미노산을 교환하여 AlphaFold 연구를 통해 확인된 10개의 핵심 위치 중 하나에 다른 아미노산을 배치했습니다. 이로 인해 표적 서열과 일치하는 부위에서 정상 Cas9과 유사한 활성을 가진 변이를 발견할 수 있었고, 비표적 활성 비율은 28%에서 5%로 떨어졌습니다. 연구진이 다른 가이드 RNA를 사용했을 때도 유사한 결과가 나왔다. 또한 이 접근법이 DNA와 가이드 RNA 조합을 인식하기 위해 다른 Cas 단백질(Cas12)을 사용하는 유사한 시스템에서도 효과가 있음을 보여주었습니다.)

As mentioned above, other research teams have used different approaches, such as directed evolution, to develop Cas9 variants that are less prone to off-target editing. When tested against these variants, the newly designed versions tended to produce similar or even slightly better activity and specificity. The big difference here is that the changes identified by this approach may be somewhat more specific to a given guide RNA/mismatch combination rather than more generally effective.
(앞서 언급했듯이, 다른 연구팀들은 방향성 진화와 같은 다양한 접근법을 사용하여 오프타겟 편집에 덜 취약한 Cas9 변종을 개발해왔습니다. 이 변이들과 비교했을 때, 새로 설계된 버전들은 비슷하거나 약간 더 나은 활성과 특이성을 보였습니다. 여기서 큰 차이점은 이 접근법으로 확인된 변화가 일반적으로 효과적이기보다는 특정 가이드 RNA/미스매칭 조합에 더 특이적일 수 있다는 점입니다.)

Of course, some of the individual changes identified here could potentially be combined with those in the previously developed Cas9 versions for even greater improvements, although that wasn’t tested here.
(물론 여기서 언급된 일부 개별 변경 사항은 이전에 개발된 Cas9 버전과 결합해 더 큰 개선을 가져올 수 있지만, 이 부분은 여기서 테스트되지 않았습니다.)

In any case, the work is potentially useful because it describes a general method for producing gene-editing systems tailored to prevent known off-target events. If that ends up being a bottleneck in developing a therapy, this work could be a significant breakthrough. But the researchers also suggest that the approach would be useful more generally for fine-tuning protein-DNA interactions, which could have applications far beyond gene editing.
(어쨌든 이 연구는 알려진 오프타겟 사건을 방지하기 위해 맞춤형 유전자 편집 시스템을 만드는 일반적인 방법을 설명하기 때문에 잠재적으로 유용하다. 만약 이것이 치료 개발의 병목 지점이 된다면, 이 연구는 중요한 돌파구가 될 수 있습니다. 하지만 연구진은 이 접근법이 단백질-DNA 상호작용을 미세 조정하는 데 더 널리 유용할 것이라고도 제안하며, 이는 유전자 편집을 넘어 훨씬 더 많은 응용 분야를 가질 수 있습니다.)

Nature, 2026. DOI: 10.1038/s41586-026-10794-z ( About DOIs ).
(네이처, 2026. DOI: 10.1038/s41586-026-10794-z (DOI 관련).)

item.title: European Union grants US request to restrict satellite images of Iran War region (유럽연합, 이란 전쟁 지역의 위성 이미지 제한 요청을 수락하다)
item.description:
New delay on Copernicus satellite pics comes as US ramps up war with Iran again.
(미국이 다시 이란과의 전쟁을 강화하면서 코페르니쿠스 위성 사진의 새로운 지연이 발생했다.)

The European Union has begun delaying the release of satellite images showing shipping lanes near the Strait of Hormuz by 24 hours. The move comes in response to an earlier US government request and coincides with the Trump administration ramping up the war with Iran once again.
(유럽연합은 호르무즈 해협 인근의 해상 항로를 보여주는 위성 이미지 공개를 24시간 연기하기 시작했다. 이 조치는 이전 미국 정부의 요청에 대한 대응이며, 트럼프 행정부가 다시 한 번 이란과의 전쟁을 강화하는 시기와 맞물린다.)

The unusual change in the free and open data policy for Europe’s Copernicus Earth observation program was revealed by Space News , which reviewed a copy of the decision made by the Council of the EU on July 13. The ordered delay applies to images taken by Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 satellites and covers the Gulf of Oman region that includes shipping lanes leading to and from the contested Strait of Hormuz.
(유럽의 코페르니쿠스 지구 관측 프로그램의 자유롭고 개방된 데이터 정책의 이례적인 변화는 7월 13일 EU 이사회가 내린 결정문 사본을 검토한 스페이스 뉴스에 의해 공개되었습니다. 이 지연 명령은 센티넬-1과 센티넬-2 위성에서 촬영된 이미지에 적용되며, 오만 지역과 호르무즈 해협으로 오가는 항로를 포함한다.)

The US government first requested that the European Union restrict Copernicus satellite imagery on May 26, according to the decision document seen by Space News. That request occurred during a shaky ceasefire period for the war that began on April 8 and ended on July 8, when the US military resumed a broader campaign of military strikes following an announcement by President Donald Trump.
(미국 정부는 5월 26일 유럽연합에 코페르니쿠스 위성 이미지 제한을 처음으로 요청했다고 스페이스 뉴스가 입수한 결정 문서가 전했다. 이 요청은 4월 8일 시작되어 7월 8일 끝난 불안정한 휴전 기간 중에 이루어졌으며, 도널드 트럼프 대통령의 발표 이후 미군이 더 광범위한 군사 공습을 재개했다.)

Satellite imagery has played important military and open source intelligence roles during the war that began with the United States and Israel attacking Iran on February 28. The US military and US intelligence agencies have continually used their satellite constellations to monitor Iranian activity during the war. Meanwhile, Iran has turned to Chinese satellite imagery to gain a similar advantage in striking US military bases and other targets.
(위성 이미지는 2월 28일 미국과 이스라엘이 이란을 공격하면서 시작된 전쟁 동안 군사 및 오픈 소스 정보 분야에서 중요한 역할을 해왔다. 미국 군과 정보기관은 전쟁 중 이란의 활동을 감시하기 위해 위성 별자리를 지속적으로 사용해 왔다. 한편, 이란은 미군 기지와 기타 목표물을 타격하는 데 있어 중국 위성 영상을 활용해 유사한 우위를 확보하고 있다.)

The modern rise of commercial satellite imagery and free public resources such as Europe’s Copernicus satellite imagery has also enabled news agencies and open source intelligence researchers to provide additional transparency on conflicts around the world. But US satellite firms such as Planet Labs and Vantor have largely restricted imagery related to the ongoing Iran war after the US government raised concerns about security risks.
(상업용 위성 이미지와 유럽의 코페르니쿠스 위성 이미지와 같은 무료 공공 자원의 현대적 부상은 뉴스 기관과 오픈 소스 정보 연구자들이 전 세계 분쟁에 대해 추가적인 투명성을 제공할 수 있게 했습니다. 하지만 미국 정부가 보안 위험에 대한 우려를 제기한 이후 Planet Labs와 Vantor 같은 미국 위성 기업들은 현재 진행 중인 이란 전쟁과 관련된 영상을 대체로 제한하고 있다.)

Such restrictions have forced journalists and researchers to rely more heavily on alternatives such as the free Copernicus satellite images and European firms that provide commercial satellite imagery. For example, the independent investigative journalism group Bellingcat released an open source tool that uses Copernicus Sentinel-1 satellite imagery to map possible war damage in Iran and the Gulf region.
(이러한 제한 때문에 언론인과 연구자들은 무료 코페르니쿠스 위성 이미지나 상업용 위성 사진을 제공하는 유럽 기업 같은 대안에 더 많이 의존하게 되었습니다. 예를 들어, 독립 탐사 저널리즘 단체인 벨링캣은 코페르니쿠스 센티넬-1 위성 이미지를 활용해 이란과 걸프 지역의 전쟁 피해 가능성을 지도화하는 오픈 소스 도구를 공개했습니다.)

Similarly, The New York Times and Washington Post have relied on Copernicus satellite imagery to investigate the extent of damage to US military bases and radar installations from Iranian missile and drone strikes. Such reporting comes at a time when the Pentagon under Trump’s administration has become less willing to share information about US military casualties or damage to military assets during the war.
(마찬가지로 뉴욕타임스와 워싱턴포스트는 이란의 미사일 및 드론 공격으로 미군 기지와 레이더 시설에 피해가 얼마나 심한지 조사하기 위해 코페르니쿠스 위성 이미지를 활용했다. 이러한 보도는 트럼프 행정부 하에서 미군 사상자나 군사 자산 피해에 관한 정보를 공유하는 데 덜 적극적으로 변한 시점에 나온 것이다.)

The 24-hour delay in the release of Copernicus satellite imagery is less onerous than US satellite firms’ restrictions and would still allow journalists and researchers to monitor the war.
(코페르니쿠스 위성 이미지 공개에 24시간 지연되는 것은 미국 위성 회사의 제한보다 덜 가혹하며, 언론인과 연구자들이 전쟁을 감시할 수 있게 한다.)

But the new restriction does create additional friction in providing timely transparency around what is happening. The potentially widening war has already killed thousands of people and created a global energy shock from ongoing disruptions to the Strait of Hormuz shipping lanes—not to mention already costing the United States more than $37 billion , with Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth requesting another $70 billion.
(하지만 새로운 제한은 현재 상황에 대해 시기적절한 투명성을 제공하는 데 추가적인 마찰을 야기합니다. 전쟁이 확대될 가능성은 이미 수천 명을 사망자로 몰아넣었고, 호르무즈 해협 해상 교통로에 지속적인 혼란이 일어나 전 세계적인 에너지 충격을 초래했으며, 미국은 이미 370억 달러 이상의 비용을 초래했으며, 국방장관 피트 헤그세스는 추가로 700억 달러를 요청했다.)

item.title: Judge rebuffs Trump admin demand for phone records from NYT reporters (판사, 뉴욕타임스 기자들의 전화 기록 요구를 트럼프 행정부의 거부)
item.description:
“We can quash the subpoenas, or you could withdraw the subpoenas,” judge told US.
(판사는 "소환장을 무효화할 수도 있고, 소환장을 철회할 수도 있다"고 말했다.)

After criticism from a federal judge, the Department of Justice yesterday withdrew demands for phone records and grand jury testimony from New York Times reporters who wrote about security concerns related to the Air Force One jet donated to Trump by Qatar.
(연방 판사의 비판 이후, 법무부는 어제 카타르가 트럼프에게 기증한 에어포스 원 전투기와 관련된 보안 우려를 다룬 뉴욕타임스 기자들의 전화 기록과 대배심 증언 요구를 철회했다.)

It was a setback in the Trump administration’s attempts to unmask journalists’ confidential sources. US District Judge Arun Subramanian “grilled Justice Department lawyers for nearly an hour over their handling of the subpoenas” during a hearing on Thursday, The New York Times wrote .
(이는 트럼프 행정부가 기자들의 비밀 소스를 밝히려는 시도에 큰 타격이었다. 뉴욕 타임스는 목요일 심리에서 미국 지방법원 판사 아룬 수브라마니안이 소환장 처리 방식에 대해 법무부 변호사들을 거의 한 시간 동안 심문했다고 보도했다.)

“Either we can quash the subpoenas, or you could withdraw the subpoenas,” Subramanian reportedly told Sean Buckley, chief counsel for the US attorney in New York’s southern district.
("우리가 소환장을 무효화하거나, 당신이 소환장을 철회할 수 있다"고 수브라마니언은 뉴욕 남부 지구 미국 검찰청 수석 법률고문 션 버클리에게 말했다고 전해진다.)

Subramanian reportedly said during the hearing that subpoenas to reporters “are not the first thing you do—they are the last thing you do,” and that “it’s a matter of basic compliance with the law.” Government lawyers agreed to withdraw the subpoenas during the hearing.
(수브라마니안은 청문회에서 기자들에게 소환장을 발부하는 것이 "가장 먼저 하는 일이 아니라 마지막으로 하는 일"이며 "법을 기본적으로 준수하는 문제"라고 말했다고 전해진다. 정부 변호인단은 청문회에서 소환장을 철회하는 데 동의했다.)

“As stated on the record during the July 23, 2026, hearing, the Government has voluntarily withdrawn the challenged subpoenas, including the subpoenas issued to the journalists as well as the third-party subpoenas. Those subpoenas are null and void. As a result, the motions to quash are moot,” Subramanian wrote in an order yesterday.
("2026년 7월 23일 청문회에서 기록에 명시된 바와 같이, 정부는 언론인들에게 발부된 소환장과 제3자 소환장을 포함해 자발적으로 이의가 제기된 소환장을 철회했습니다. 그 소환장은 무효입니다. 따라서 무효화 신청은 무의미해졌다."고 수브라마니안은 어제 명령서에서 썼다.)

The NYT reported on Monday that the US government sought phone and text messaging records of NYT journalists and their relatives, including one reporter’s mother and two reporters’ spouses. This was in addition to subpoenas demanding that reporters testify before a federal grand jury.
(뉴욕 타임스는 월요일에 미국 정부가 뉴욕 타임스 기자들과 그 가족들, 그리고 한 명의 기자의 어머니와 두 명의 배우자를 포함한 전화 및 문자 메시지 기록을 요청했다고 보도했다. 이는 기자들이 연방 대배심에 증언하도록 요구하는 소환장에 더해진 조치였습니다.)

On July 15, the NYT filed a motion to quash the subpoenas seeking grand jury testimony. The motion called the demands “a brazen effort to intimidate the press into abandoning its critical, constitutionally protected role.” The motion said armed federal agents served the subpoenas at the journalists’ homes, ordering them to appear before a grand jury within three business days.
(7월 15일, 뉴욕타임스는 대배심 증언을 요구하는 소환장 기각 신청서를 제출했다. 이 동의안은 이 요구를 "언론이 헌법적으로 보호받는 중요한 역할을 포기하도록 위협하려는 노골적인 시도"라고 규정했다. 신청서에 따르면 무장 연방 요원들이 기자들의 집에 소환장을 전달하며, 3영업일 이내에 대배심에 출석하라고 명령했다.)

“The Federal Bureau of Investigation Director [Kash Patel] orchestrated this activity from within the White House, in close coordination with top Administration officials and in response to the President’s anger over the reporting,” the motion said.
("연방수사국장[카시 파텔]은 백악관 내부에서 이 활동을 주도하며, 행정부 고위 관계자들과 긴밀히 협력하고, 대통령의 보도에 대한 분노에 대응했다"고 동의서에 적혀 있다.)

Two days after this motion was filed, the government revealed in a call with NYT counsel that it also served subpoenas on phone providers for call records, according to a July 18 filing . In the newer filing, the NYT asked the court “to quash the newly-disclosed grand jury subpoenas served on third-party phone service providers on July 10, July 14, and July 16, 2026, for records associated with the Journalists.”
(이 신청서가 제출된 지 이틀 후, 정부는 뉴욕타임스 변호사와의 통화에서 통화 기록을 위해 전화 제공업체에 소환장도 발부했다고 7월 18일 제출 서류에 밝혔다. 최근 제출된 서류에서 뉴욕타임스는 법원에 "2026년 7월 10일, 7월 14일, 7월 16일에 제3자 전화 서비스 제공업체에 발부된 기자들과 관련된 기록에 대한 대배심 소환장을 무효화해 달라"고 요청했다.)

During Subramanian’s questioning of DOJ lawyers, “the government acknowledged factual errors in its filings. It conceded that it had omitted significant information—including that the case pertained to journalists’ records—when it asked a different federal judge to prevent a phone company from disclosing a record request,” the NYT reported.
(서브라마니언이 법무부 변호사들을 심문하는 동안, "정부는 제출 서류에 사실적 오류를 인정했다. 뉴욕 타임스는 사건이 언론인 기록과 관련된 중요한 정보를 누락했다는 점을 인정했다.)

Buckley had “argued that the nature of The Times’s reporting on sensitive national security matters had allowed for an exception to standard procedures,” but “he struggled to identify the precise legal rationale for that exception when the judge pressed him,” the NYT article said.
(버클리는 "타임스의 민감한 국가 안보 문제에 대한 보도의 성격이 표준 절차에 예외를 허용했다"고 주장했지만, "판사가 그를 압박했을 때 그 예외에 대한 정확한 법적 근거를 찾기 어려웠다"고 뉴욕타임스 기사는 전했다.)

Buckley apparently admitted that the subpoenas shouldn’t have sought phone records of reporters’ relatives. “Mr. Buckley also acknowledged that the phone record subpoenas had inadvertently encompassed relatives of the Times reporters—including the mother of one and the spouses of two others—calling it an error and ‘a consequence of trying to move quickly,’” the NYT wrote.
(버클리는 소환장이 기자 가족의 전화 기록을 요구해서는 안 된다고 인정한 것으로 보인다. "버클리 씨는 또한 전화 기록 소환장이 실수로 타임스 기자들의 친척들—한 명의 어머니와 두 명의 배우자를 포함해—까지 포함했다는 점을 인정하며, 이를 실수이자 '서두르려다 한 결과'라고 표현했다"고 뉴욕타임스는 썼다.)

The Trump administration lashed out at the judge after the hearing. “This judge threatened our attorneys with sanctions unless subpoenas were withdrawn, and blocked us from presenting the meticulous process of this investigation,” a DOJ spokesperson said in a statement provided to Ars today.
(트럼프 행정부는 심리 후 판사를 강하게 비난했다. "이 판사는 소환장이 철회되지 않으면 우리 변호사들에게 제재를 가하겠다고 위협했고, 이 조사의 세심한 절차를 제시하는 것을 막았다,"고 법무부 대변인이 오늘 Ars에 제공한 성명에서 말했다.)

“The grand jury has a right to hear testimony from all material witnesses in a federal criminal investigation,” the DOJ statement continued. “This judge’s conduct overrides clear longstanding principles and common sense—blocking the grand jury from receiving core evidence in a national security investigation. Make no mistake, this investigation remains ongoing, and we will pursue justice against those threatening national security by leaking classified information, a serious federal crime.”
(법무부 성명은 이어서 "대배심은 연방 형사 수사에서 모든 중요한 증인들의 증언을 들을 권리가 있다"고 덧붙였다. "이 판사의 행위는 명확한 오랜 원칙과 상식을 무시합니다—국가 안보 수사에서 대배심이 핵심 증거를 받는 것을 막는 것입니다. 분명히 말씀드리자면, 이 조사는 계속 진행 중이며, 우리는 국가 안보를 위협하는 기밀 정보 유출자에 대해 정의를 실현할 것입니다. 이는 심각한 연방 범죄입니다.")

NYT newsroom lawyer David McCraw issued a statement calling the hearing “an important affirmation of our country’s commitment to a free press. We are pleased that the government finally conceded that the subpoenas violated the law, but they should never have been issued in the first place.”
(뉴욕타임스 뉴스룸 변호사 데이비드 맥크로우는 이번 청문회를 "우리나라가 자유 언론에 대한 의지를 확인하는 중요한 자리"라고 평가하는 성명을 발표했다. 정부가 마침내 소환장이 법을 위반했다는 점을 인정한 것은 기쁘지만, 애초에 소환장이 발부되어서는 안 됐다."고 말했다.)

The NYT motion to quash said that after Trump accepted the Boeing jet from Qatar, “concerns were immediately raised about the ethical implications of accepting a $400 million gift from a foreign government, the costs to American taxpayers of retrofitting a commercial jet to serve as a ‘flying White House’—with all the necessary communications, security, and support capabilities—and the national security implications of using a foreign-donated aircraft for that purpose.”
(뉴욕타임스의 취소 신청서에 따르면, 트럼프가 카타르에서 온 보잉 제트기를 수락한 직후, "외국 정부로부터 4억 달러 기부를 받는 것의 윤리적 문제, 상업용 제트기를 '비행하는 백악관'으로 개조하는 데 드는 미국 납세자들의 비용—필요한 모든 통신과 보안이 갖춰져 있다는 점에 대한 우려가 즉시 제기되었다. 지원 능력과 외국에서 기증된 항공기를 그 목적에 사용할 경우 국가 안보에 미치는 영향에 대해 설명한다.")

The NYT motion said the paper’s reporting on the topic “was manifestly in the public interest. It contributed to the public’s knowledge about the workings of the Executive Branch, the President’s dealings with foreign nations, and the safety of an aircraft that transports the President and many other public officials, reporters, and guests.”
(뉴욕타임스 동의안은 해당 주제에 대한 신문의 보도가 "명백히 공익에 부합한다"고 밝혔다. 이 행사는 행정부의 운영, 대통령의 외국과의 교류, 그리고 대통령과 많은 공무원, 기자, 손님을 수송하는 항공기의 안전성에 대해 대중에게 알리는 데 기여했다.")

In January, the FBI seized devices from a Washington Post reporter who had built up a contact list of 1,100 current and former government employees. The government said it was unable to access data from the iPhone because it was protected by Apple’s Lockdown Mode, but it did access the reporter’s work MacBook Pro by compelling her to unlock it with her fingerprint.
(1월에 FBI는 워싱턴 포스트 기자로부터 1,100명의 현직 및 전직 정부 직원 연락처 목록을 구축한 기기를 압수했다. 정부는 아이폰이 애플의 락다운 모드로 보호되어 있어 데이터에 접근할 수 없었다고 밝혔지만, 기자의 직장용 맥북 프로에는 지문으로 잠금 해제하도록 강제해 접근했다.)

A judge ordered a halt to the FBI search of the Post reporter’s devices, and decided the court would do the search itself because the government only had probable cause to obtain a small fraction of the material it seized.
(판사는 포스트 기자의 기기에 대한 FBI 수색을 중단하라고 명령했고, 정부가 압수한 자료의 일부만을 확보할 개연성 있는 이유가 있었기 때문에 법원이 직접 수색을 진행하기로 결정했다.)
